name: Eye color meditation / visualization
lead: Eye color meditation or visualization is a practice in which people try to change the color of their irises by meditating, affirming or mentally picturing a different color. People use it hoping to end up with lighter or differently colored eyes, a feature many consider a standout part of the face, without cosmetic lenses or surgery. It circulates in wellness and self-transformation circles and in some appearance-focused online communities as a free, non-invasive option.

Practitioners usually frame it in terms of manifestation, the New Thought idea that focused thoughts and affirmations bring about matching outcomes. Wikipedia traces the roots of that idea to 19th-century mind-over-body ideas and to later popularizers, and states that there is no empirical scientific evidence supporting the law of attraction [3].

Reference works on eye color describe it as determined mainly by the amount and distribution of melanin in the iris, with the HERC2-OCA2 region on chromosome 15 and several other genes contributing [1][2]. Neither encyclopedia article mentions meditation or visualization as a recognized influence on iris color [1][2], and no published clinical study has tested the practice.

paras: Practitioners describe sitting quietly and imagining the iris taking on a target color, often combined with affirmations and repeated over weeks or months. Accounts of the technique are typically framed in terms of mind-body or manifestation ideas rather than any specified physiological pathway.
Wikipedia describes advocates of manifestation as often pairing affirmations and creative visualization with the idea of feeling that a desired change has already happened [3].

sections.h: What is known about eye color
paras: Eye color depends on the pigment melanin in the iris stroma and on how light scatters within the tissue. Brown eyes contain more stromal melanin; blue eyes contain little, and their color arises from light scattering rather than blue pigment. Genetically it is a polygenic trait, with OCA2 and HERC2 the best-characterized genes [1].

Eye color can change naturally in some circumstances. Many infants are born with blue-gray eyes that darken as melanin accumulates, usually stabilizing within the first year, and a 1997 study of white Americans reported that about 17 percent of children's eyes changed color by adulthood, with similar numbers lightening and darkening [1][2]. Pregnancy-related temporary darkening has been described, and sudden or marked change in adults can accompany medical conditions such as glaucoma, cataract or iris atrophy [2]. Certain medications, such as some prostaglandin analogue eye drops, can increase iris pigmentation [1].
Grokipedia's article on eye color states that mood or emotional state does not change the iris itself, although emotions can alter perceived color by changing pupil size [2].

A 2016 meta-analysis of 78 neuroimaging studies of meditation found distinct patterns of brain activation across styles such as focused attention, mantra recitation and open monitoring [4]. That work examines brain activity and does not address changes to the eye.

No studies found. No published human study has tested whether meditation, visualization or affirmation changes iris color or melanin content. Separately, ophthalmology bodies have issued warnings about procedures and products that claim to change eye color, such as keratopigmentation and over-the-counter color-changing drops, citing risks of vision-threatening complications [2].

card.summary: Trying to change iris color by meditating or picturing a new shade; no study has tested it and iris color is set by melanin and genes.
card.aka: Eye color visualization, manifesting eye color change
card.note: No published human studies; physical methods of changing eye color carry documented risks and are a separate topic.

quick.overview:
Eye color meditation is the idea that focused visualization or affirmation can gradually change the color of your irises. It is shared in wellness and self-improvement spaces as a free, non-invasive option.

Reference works describe iris color as determined by melanin and genetics, and do not list meditation among the known influences. No clinical study has tested the practice.
quick.mechanism: Practitioners sit and imagine a target eye color, often with affirmations, over an extended period. No physiological mechanism linking this to iris melanin has been described in published research; known natural changes occur through development, hormones, medications or disease.
quick.risks: The practice itself is non-invasive and no direct harms have been reported. Ophthalmology bodies warn about other eye-color-changing products and procedures, and sudden real changes in eye color can accompany medical conditions.

chain: Sit quietly and picture or affirm a target iris color
Practitioners hope for lighter or different-colored irises
angle.text: People practice it hoping to change how their eyes look, aiming at a lighter or different shade at no cost and without any procedure. The practice is mental only, and its proponents describe results in terms of manifestation rather than a physical pathway.
